Rooms.Name: A Scraggly Trail
Rooms.Description:
This trail slopes up and away from the main road to the west. At
points the trail seems to fade into obscurity against the gray stone
and near-gray mountain grass prevalent here. The trail leads generally
eastward and up higher into the rocky ground. There is a sign here,
seemingly out-of-place in this rough country.

Exits.Description: You can barely make out a faded trail across rocky ground.
A trail through a dense forest.

Rooms.Name: A Scraggly Trail
Rooms.Description:
What could barely be called a trail leads west back down the
mountainside, and down into a very small valley where a small house
sits in the middle of a well-groomed yard. The door to the house is 
open and inviting, welcoming you for a visit.

Exits.Description: A faint trail leads west over a scraggly mountainside.

Watch your step!  A steep slope lies between you and a lovely small
valley.

Rooms.Name: A Groomed Path
Rooms.Description:
You are standing in the western end of a very, very small valley,
just about room enough for the one house standing to your east. You can
see from here that the door to the cozy cottage is open and inviting,
but the interior seems very dark. A path bordered by shrubberies leads
up to the structure, and ends where you are standing; right by the
easiest path back up into the mountains.

Exits.Description: A somewhat overgrown path leads up to the door of a cottage.

If you scramble up the path you will be on the trail into the
mountains.

Rooms.Name: Outside a House
Rooms.Description:
The path you are on leads from the front door of the cottage to your
east, to the edge of the small valley to the west. The building seems
quiet... almost too quiet. A small voice in the back of your head, the
same voice that has saved your life on countless occasions, seems to be
telling you that something is very, very wrong here.

Exits.Description: It's a normal front door to a house.
A path bordered in green shrubs leads to a steep slope.

Rooms.Name: Smithery
Rooms.Description:
Devastation greets your eyes. The forge has been blasted apart,
along with most of the back door. Hammers, tongs, and anvils lie about 
in one gigantic mess, and the smith's bed smolders yet. This place has
been utterly wrecked and blasted apart, by more than one man you 
would think from all the tracks in the dust...

Exits.Description: What used to be a door leads to what used to be a small garden.
Some odd tracks ... three sets ...
It's a normal front door.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Ha!  Lucky, you were always lucky!

   Under the pillow is a half-written letter, unaddressed.  The bits of
text that aren't smudged, burnt, and smeared tell tale of the
smith/mage Gabadiel's masterwork: a sword of unequaled power, and two 
swords that came before, discarded as 'Not quite what I was 
working towards'.

   Looking around, you notice a distinct lack of any swords.  You think
you may have a motive now...
Three sets of prints lead out where the back door used to stand.

Rooms.Name: A Small Garden
Rooms.Description:
This garden was probably once kept orderly and weedless.
Unfortunately, it seems someone has been careless with a fireball.
There's nothing here now but blast-marks and ashes, and the remains of
a trail leading to the east edge of this tiny valley.

Exits.Description: What used to be a door leads to a small house

Rooms.Name: Mountain Ridge
Rooms.Description:
You are standing on a ridge in the mountains, just east of a very
small valley. You spot a tiny cottage sitting in the center of the
valley, and the ridge continues south. Looking at the sheer drops to
the north and west, you consider not taking those directions.

Exits.Description: Some faint tracks in the dirt lead south.
The sad shell of a smithy lies just west of where you are standing.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: The tracks lead south.

Rooms.Name: Mountain Ridge
Rooms.Description:
The mountain range continues north from here, and widens out into a
small plateau just to your south. Going east and west from here would
be a bad idea, considering the steepness of the drop. From this height,
you have a fairly good panoramic view to the south, including what
appears to be a small mountain village to your south and west, and 
a tall, ominous peak westwards from here.

Exits.Description: Perhaps it would be better to track the tracks back the way they came!

Civilization! It's still off in the distance, but you can see a small,
boring little village from here.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: They lead south.

Rooms.Name: Diverging Paths
Rooms.Description:
You are standing on a small plateau in the mountains, just south of
a ridge that leads northwards through the rocky area. To the east,
south, and west are gentle slopes leading down into different areas of
the mountains. A giant, dark peak looks down over you to the west,
looking quite spooky indeed!

Exits.Description: A difficult path leads north, along a rocky mountain ridge.
You are right near a small cluster of buildings that may be a town!

The little path twists down a steep slope, allowing you to see nothing
of its destination.
A very rocky trail up yet another mountain.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The three sets of tracks split up here, one west, one 
east, one south.

Rooms.Name: A Steep Slope
Rooms.Description:
This slopes leads down and to the west from here. Up above, you see
a plateau at the southern end of a long mountain ridge. Surprisingly,
there seems to be signs of traffic in this area, leading into the large
depression here. The going looks somewhat dangerous, and you decide to
exercise a little caution.

Exits.Description: A gentle slope lies north of you.

In the near distance there is a large depression, with some tracks in
the dust.
A gentle slope leads up to an intersection of sorts.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
A few boot prints lead way in the dust here.  There's definitely
traffic here, but this area is not what you would call well-traveled.

Rooms.Name: Small Plateau
Rooms.Description:
You are standing upon another mini-plateau, bordered by a sheer wall
of rock to the north. You can climb up the slope to the east, or
continue along the flat area to the west. Another slope leads downwards
to the south, looking unsafe but climbable.

Exits.Description: The dusty rocks might help you climb up this gentle slope.

Loose rock and shale head down a steep slope, making it a dangerous
climb.
The ground flattens out for a bit, amazingly.

Rooms.Name: Small Plateau
Rooms.Description:
This plateau ends here, with a steep drop-off to the south, and a
solid wall of rock to the north. Eastwards the plateau continues, and
you think you can climb up the steep rocky slope just west of here. You
are afforded a good view of the lower regions of this depression, and
you think you spot what might be a cave south and down from here...

Exits.Description: You can walk easily eastwards, along a flat stretch of plateau.

The land takes another turn ... up this time.  The ground is hard and
rocky.

Rooms.Name: Rocky Slope
Rooms.Description:
This slope is fairly treacherous, but looks to be somewhat safer to
the north. East the slope leads down to a small plateau that also looks
considerably safer than your other choices. The shale under your feet
slips badly, and you are almost thrown off balance; this is no place to
be without mountaineering equipment.

Rooms.Name: Overlook
Rooms.Description:
You are standing on a point outcropping with a beautiful view of the
mountains to the north. Far below, you see what appears to be a
foot-path climb up to the central mountain, a peak that looks dark and
disturbing. You get very bad vibes from that mountain for some reason,
and it doesn't seem like a very good idea to try to find a way to get
there. The only safe way to leave this overlook is to the south.

Rooms.Name: Rocky Slope
Rooms.Description:
You slip and slide your way across the steep ground, trying
desperately to keep your balance. You can climb up to a small plateau
to the north from here, or carefully head down to the floor of the
depression to the west. You're not sure which is safer...

Rooms.Name: Depression Floor
Rooms.Description:
A small path leads south here, away from the rocky slope leading up
to the east. A small spring burbles here, evidently the cause of much
of the traffic.  Looking up, you see sheer rock walls surrounding much
of the depression, making an effective fortress of this place.

Rooms.Name: Depression Floor
Rooms.Description:
The small path you are standing on leads north, and east into what
appears to be a large cave hollowed out of the mountainside. The whole
place seems quiet, too quiet in fact. Your little adventurer's
intuition is busily warning you of traps.

Exits.Description: A dark cave leads eastwards, full of mystery.

Rooms.Name: Cave Entrance
Rooms.Description:
A cave leads into the heart of the mountainside, well-lit by sconces
upon the walls. A large rock sits by the side here, near a small
firepit.  Debris litters the area; rabbit bones, half of a broken
whetstone, and random litter.  The ground is devoid of grass, and well
trodden by many pairs of boots.  Strange that someone should live so
deep in the mountains...

Rooms.Name: Cave Passageway
Rooms.Description:
You are near the entrance of the cave. The outside light streams in
from the west, accompanied by a slight breeze, making the flames in the
sconces flutter a bit and throw strange shadows upon the walls. This
passageway heads north and south from here, each way seeming dark and
stuffy compared to outdoors.  From the tracks in the floor, you guess
that the north is the more used.

Rooms.Name: Cave Passageway
Rooms.Description:
The passage turns here, one end leading south, towards the cave's
entrance, and east -- that much deeper into the mountain. The light
sconces keep the area bright enough to see, but not nearly bright
enough for you to be quite comfortable in this strange place. From 
far off you hear the echoes of what sound to be voices.

Rooms.Name: Cave Passageway
Rooms.Description:
This twisty passage leads east and west from here. Eastwards you
hear the unmistakable sounds of low voices. The echoes seem to be 
playing funny effects on you, however, and you are not sure from 
how far off these voices might be coming.

Rooms.Name: Cave Passageway
Rooms.Description:
The passage you are standing in turns west and south from here. One
of the sconces here is out, making this area extremely dark and hard to
see in.  You do see lights from the south, however, seemingly brighter
than the sconces you've seen along the walls so far.

Rooms.Name: Cave Passageway
Rooms.Description:
This is a T-intersection in the cave passageway, the north leading
back towards the cave's entrance (you think!), the west leading towards
a well-lighted area. Eastwards the passageway continues uninvitingly
into the shadowy recesses of the mountain. The echoes of voices are
confusing you a bit, and you are not sure whether you should try to
remain quiet or not.

Rooms.Name: Cave
Rooms.Description:
Many sconces line the walls here, casting light on some weapon racks
and chests of armor. Everything is neat, orderly, and actually
well-dusted.  Someone cares for these items... frequently it seems.

Rooms.Name: Cave Passageway
Rooms.Description:
The passageway you are in leads south and west from here. Many large
stones and rocks are on the floor of the cave, making walking difficult
in the dim light from the sconces on the walls. You hear the continued
echo of voices, seemingly fainter now. Must be the strange acoustics of
this place...

Rooms.Name: Cave Passageway
Rooms.Description:
The cave twists around like a coiled snake, leading east and north
from here. You begin to wonder if your orientations are still correct.
That worries you for some reason.

Rooms.Name: Cave Passageway
Rooms.Description:
You can head north and west through the cave passageways here, both
ways dimly lit by the ever-present sconces on the walls. The echoes you
heard earlier seem to be getting louder, and seem to be coming from the
northern passage. You feel a bit chilled from the cooled cave air and
shiver a bit in the faint whisper of a breeze. This place is a little
too eerie and dark to be comfortable in.

Rooms.Name: Cave Passageway
Rooms.Description:
The echoes are growing louder, and seem to be coming from the
northern end of this corridor. Southwards you see the tunnel continue
right before yet another bend in the passageway. You spot a small piece
of red cloth torn against a sharp rock jutting out from the passage's
side. It looks like silk, very nice in fact.

Rooms.Name: Cave Passageway
Rooms.Description:
The main passageway leads south from here, and a smaller cave tunnel
leads away to the west. Two large boulders sit against the wall, wiped
clean of dirt and grime. A paper food wrapper has been trodden under
several pairs of feet here; at best guess, you'd say this would
probably be a guard post.

Rooms.Name: End of the Passageway
Rooms.Description:
The cave passageway ends abruptly here to the north in a large
wooden door set into the stone walls. The craftsmanship is superb! 
You can also head back to the main passage to the west, where there 
seems to be more light than here. An echo from down the passage makes 
you wonder for a moment if you're being followed, but you see nothing 
there...

Exits.Description: It's a sturdy wooden door.

Rooms.Name: Cavern
Rooms.Description:
This natural cavern has been turned into a combination
office/storeroom. A small brook rushes through the south wall, and
flows back into the west wall through a tiny hole. Boxes and crates are
stacked against the walls, and a beat up oaken desk stands near the
door stacked with papers written upon by an unsteady hand. Some large
lanterns keep the place very well lighted.

Exits.Description: It's a sturdy wooden door.

Rooms.Name: Cave Passageway
Rooms.Description:
You are standing south of the main entrance to this cave. The
passage you are in continues south, very badly lit along its length by
the sconces lining the walls every fifteen feet or so. From somewhere
deep in the recesses of the cave, you hear a faint, rhythmic thumping
sound distorted by the passage's strange acoustics.

Rooms.Name: Cave Passageway
Rooms.Description:
You are standing at the southern bend of this passage, able to head
east and north from here. The rock around you echoes the sound of
far-off pounding to you, making the place seem somehow alive, with a
heartbeat. This place is fairly eerie, now that you come to think of
it.

Rooms.Name: Cave Passageway
Rooms.Description:
The passageway makes a U-turn here, heading north and westwards to
the other side of the 'U'. The air seems humid and hard to breathe.
Some algae grows near the floor in the slick spots, giving a definite
subtle smell of rot to the air.

Rooms.Name: Cave Passageway
Rooms.Description:
The tunnel twists to the south and east from here, its dark length
seemingly dismal and lifeless. A faint thumping sound reverberates from
the walls, making you perk your ears for the direction of the noise.

Rooms.Name: Cave Passageway
Rooms.Description:
This area darker than the rest of the passageway, due to the fact
that the sconces along the walls stop abruptly here. The way to the
south is completely dark, in direct contrast to the tunnels to the
west.  You peer hard to the south, but can make out nothing in the
impenetrable darkness. And still that distant thumping impinges on your
consciousness...

Rooms.Name: Cave Passageway
Rooms.Description:
You are standing in a north-south tunnel carved naturally through
the stone of the mountain. To the north the tunnel is lighted by
sconces along the wall, banishing the deep, deep darkness you now stand
in. To the south you can see nothing. A deep thumping noise seems to be
getting louder and louder as you stand here, coming from somewhere deep
inside.

Rooms.Name: Cave Passageway
Rooms.Description:
The passageway switches directions again in the dark gloom of the
mountain, heading to the north and east from here. As you round the
corner, a trick of the acoustics make the deep thrumming and pounding
you've been hearing sound as if its coming from two feet away! Very
unsettling.

Rooms.Name: Cave Passageway
Rooms.Description:
The tunnel weaves around, twisting to the north and west here. The
darkness around you is near total. Ahead, you hear the sounds of
something metal banging against stone. Could someone be mining out the
tunnel, perhaps?

Rooms.Name: Cave Passageway
Rooms.Description:
A glimmer of light to the east alerts you to the fact that something
is going on in the tunnel nearby. The south exit of the tunnel leads
off into complete darkness. All around on the ground are piles of earth
and stone, making you have to wend through the tunnel carefully. Hmm.

Rooms.Name: End of Passage
Rooms.Description:
The tunnel stops abruptly here at a fissure in the stone. All around
on the ground are rocks and gravel, mined from the fissure in an
attempt to widen it enough for passage. A few pieces of paper litter
and wrappers tells you that the work here is relatively recent.

Rooms.Name: A Rocky Slope
Rooms.Description:
This treacherous slope leads ever-downward quite a ways, down to a
valley where there seems to be a small village! What a village is doing
this far from civilization, and how they survive you've no idea. From
the smoke wafting from some of the chimneys, it looks like this place
is still inhabited as well. Now if you can only get down this slope
without breaking an ankle...

Rooms.Name: A Rocky Slope
Rooms.Description:
You're slipping and sliding across this slope, trying to get to your
destination without breaking your leg or falling and shattering your
head.  Below, you spot some movement in the village, giving proof the
place is not a ghost-town. The main road of the village starts at the
bottom of the slope just to the east, and the slope continues west and
up far, far up the mountain.

Rooms.Name: Main Road
Rooms.Description:
This place leaves you very unimpressed. And bored. You are
definitely bored by this place. The people are listless, going about
their daily chores with a slowness that pains your eyes. A slope to the
west climbs up the mountainside, and two open shops made of wood and
stone are to your north and south.  East-wards this road continues.
#GThere is a small sign here. #N

Exits.Description:
The faint stench of sour ale leads you to believe this might be a
tavern.
The dusty little road continues into a dusty little town.

The interior of the squat wooden building is so dim you can't make
anything out.
The Stanneg mountains tower over you in the distance.

Rooms.Name: The Mountain Tavern
Rooms.Description:
Hmm. Looks like there's no one here, not even an bartender.
Evidently you've come during off hours, since no bar could be THIS
dull. The walls are decorated with mounted animal heads and arrows and
longbows and other hunting equipment/trophies. All of it looks rather
plain. 

#GA sign hangs in a prominent position over the bar.#N

Exits.Description: A dusty little street is right out the door

Rooms.Name: General Store
Rooms.Description:
A bored shopkeeper waves an idle hand towards his stock of stuff.
Browse, type list, buy, sell, whatever...

Exits.Description: A dusty little street is bound to take you someplace more exciting.

Rooms.Name: Main Road
Rooms.Description:
Nothing is going on in this section of village either. To the east
is an actual road intersection, and to the west you see one of the ends
of this road.  A large grassy area to the south is fenced off for a
horse corral.

Exits.Description: A few ramshackle buildings make up the little town of Stanneg.
The scent of horses and hay drifts towards you.
The great Stanneg mountains loom to the west.

Rooms.Name: Corral
Rooms.Description:
Many horses look up at you when you enter this corral. The horses
are kept in by a big wooden fence, which they seem quite happy to be
kept in by. There's usually a cowgirl around here somewhere, looking
after the horses.

Exits.Description: A dusty road passes the farm.

Rooms.Name: Intersection
Rooms.Description:
You are standing in an intersection deep in the heart of Stanneg by
the Mountains. In fact, this is the ONLY intersection anywhere in
Stanneg by the Mountain it appears. There are some buildings to the
north, and south, and east, and west. None particularly stand out from
the others.

Exits.Description: A dusty little street leads up to a house.
A small gathering of buildings makes up a boring little town.
The start of a long trail downhill through rocky farms.
The Stanneg mountains loom in the distance.

Rooms.Name: Small Road
Rooms.Description:
This road runs north through Stanneg by the Mountains, if through
would be the operative word for such a motley collection of buildings.
Westwards is a small, open-roofed building that appears to be a
farmer's market. The road you are on continues north, and comes to an
intersection just south of here.

Exits.Description: The road seems to come to an end just north of here.
A small cluster of buildings is all that remains of Stanneg.
A small farmer's market appears to be in business.

Rooms.Name: Farmer's Market
Rooms.Description:
One farmer's wife stands here, waiting for someone to buy the food
her family has grown. She looks bored, but not unhappy... no
competition!

Exits.Description: A small dusty street through town

Rooms.Name: Small Road
Rooms.Description:
The small, north-south road running through Stanneg by the Mountains
ends here, curving to become the front walk of a private home to the
east. The road runs south from this house, towards the center of the
village.

Exits.Description:
A normal, wooden front door to a normal looking home. It's nothing to
write home about.

Rooms.Name: Private Home
Rooms.Description:
The interior of this home is simple and rustic. A ladder leads up to
the loft, where the sleeping pallets are tucked away. A wood-burning
stove keeps the place well heated and cozy. A homemade rocking chair
stands crooked in the corner, draped with a old looking afghan. This
home is a nice place, very comfortable.

Exits.Description: Its a normal appearing door set in the western wall.

Rooms.Name: Small Road
Rooms.Description:
The road passes by to a stone house to the east. Smoke
rises from the chimney in a dark stream, and the windows are frosted
over with humidity. North, you see the main intersection of Stanneg. 
The road continues south.

Exits.Description: A normal looking front door made of wood.
The road continues through pastures and meadows.

Rooms.Name: Private Home
Rooms.Description:
This home strikes you as unbearably warm and uncomfortable. The
fireplace is going at a full-bonfire, a mammoth stack of firewood
beside it against the wall. The decorations seem somewhat spartan and
plain; a landscape, an old hunting bow... nothing much of interest.

Exits.Description: A normal looking wooden door.

Rooms.Name: Main Road
Rooms.Description:
The main road through Stanneg ends here at a large well that leads
deep, deep into the earth. To the north of the well is a large
building, with a large WELCOME mat outside its front door. Westwards
you see the a road intersection in the center of the tiny village.
South stands an unpretentious building with a long line of people 
apparently waiting to get into it. Around you is a rocky terrain 
in the middle of this mountain range...  not very many places else 
to go.

Exits.Description: A large set of double doors, made of wood.
A line of people stand waiting to enter a small building.
The little road continues west to an intersection and beyond.

Rooms.Name: Stanneg Inn
Rooms.Description:
This is a plainly decorated room, the main room of the Stanneg Inn.
A large arch to the west leads to a common room where food and drink
can be ordered, and a set of rickety wooden stairs lead up to the rooms
are.  A thread-bare rug lies in the middle of the floor, evidently
well-loved by a cat or two from the quantity of hair on it.

Exits.Description: A large set of double doors, made of wood.

Rooms.Name: Common Room
Rooms.Description:
A large fireplace warms this room in great waves of heat, combating
the chilling drafts emanating from the windows on the west and north
sides of this room. A few benches and tables are clustered in the
center of the room, for the use of the locals. Fairly plain, for a
frequented gathering place. 
#GA sign hangs prominently near the bartender's table.#N

Exits.Description:
The entranceway is just east of this room, an extension of the
room, really.  Quite plain.

Rooms.Name: Reception
Rooms.Description:
Short hallways lead east and west from the reception area, lined
with plain brown doors. A small table has a ledger on it, seemingly
almost unused. This area is plain and without any decoration, except
for a nice painting of (what else) a mountain hanging above the stairs
that lead back down to the inn proper.

Exits.Description: A Short Hallway leads to some rooms in the inn.
A Short hallway leads to some rooms in the Inn.

Rooms.Name: A Rocky Slope
Rooms.Description:
This slope is fairly shallow and easy to walk on, despite the loose
shale and gravel. To the east is a high ridge you could stand on, and
to the west is a flat area near two trails leading up and down into the
mountains. High above you, to your west, is that ominous, dark peak,
which seems to radiating a sense of hopelessness...

Rooms.Name: Ledge
Rooms.Description:
This ledge overlooks a small path that leads up and down from here.
Below, you see the path head down to a large flat area where a small
cottage lies nestled in the mountains, smoke rising from it in a
curling line. Above, the path seems to head towards that dark peak
piercing the sky. You notice a few boot-tracks in the earth, seemingly
to lead down towards the cottage.

Rooms.Name: Outside of a Cottage
Rooms.Description:
Now that you approach closer to the cottage, you notice that the
smoke is not coming from the chimney, but rather the gutted ruins of
the building.  Something torched this place, badly. You see no signs of
life among the wreckage. You can enter one of the particularly large
holes in the wall to the west, with caution.

Rooms.Name: Torched Cottage
Rooms.Description:
This whole place is smoldering still from whatever decided to try to
burn it to the ground. On the floor near the center of the ruined
structure is the burnt and desiccated corpse of a man, outstretched and
blackened. There's not much to see here; whatever decided to destroy
this place did it very well.

Rooms.Name: Mountain Trail
Rooms.Description:
This mountain trail leads straight up into the evil looking
mountains. High above you, one mountain peak seems to radiate danger
and fear, and the trail seems to be leading straight up to it. You
wonder if it is wise to continue this way... The trail goes even higher
up to the west, and back down to the west.

Rooms.Name: Mountain Trail
Rooms.Description:
The trail leads up even higher into the mountains to the west here.
You shiver as the cold mountain air washes over you, and your back
prickles as you wonder if anything lives up here, or anything
_dangerous_ for that matter.  Maybe heading back down to the east would
be a good idea...

Rooms.Name: Mountain Trail
Rooms.Description:
The trail leads up the side of the tallest mountain in the
range--the one that sticks up into the dark sky like a monument to
death and futility. The trail leads back to safety to the east, and
goes even higher to the west.

Rooms.Name: Near the Peak
Rooms.Description:
This is as close to the peak as you're going to get, unless you use
that tiny, tiny path leading up to your north. Up the side of the
mountain you see a great cave hollowed out, the inside pitch black. The
path leads down the mountains to your east, which seems to be the best
place to go.

Rooms.Name: Small, Dangerous Path
Rooms.Description:
This path leads up, up, up the side of the mountain, to the
evil-seeming cave. It also heads down to the south--a lot safer place
to be. In fact, you hear footsteps above your head...

Rooms.Name: Small, Dangerous Path
Rooms.Description:
Unfortunately, you realize too late that this bigger ledge that
leads north to the darkened cave is an ideal spot for an ambush. This 
ledge gives you a beautiful panoramic view of the entire mountain 
range, however. Breathtaking!

Rooms.Name: Cave Entrance
Rooms.Description:
You are standing in the entrance of a simply huge cave! The size is
stunning! All around the entrance are burnt bones and various types of
wooden and metal debris. Giant claw marks are all along the ground,
leading back deeper into the cave. Two tunnels lead off from here, one
up, one down. There are claw marks leading in either direction.

Rooms.Name: Sloping Tunnel
Rooms.Description:
The tunnels slopes up to the north deeper into the mountain. A
rather gusty breeze riffles your clothing from ahead somewhere. The
claw marks in the stone floor continue up the passage, through the
darkness.

Exits.Description: Following the claw marks take you further into the dark.

The entrance to the cave is so bright you can't see much except that
it IS the entrance.

Rooms.Name: Sloping Tunnel
Rooms.Description:
The tunnel continues its slope upwards, and the wind blows at you
even stronger yet. The claw tracks in the stone stop abruptly here,
where there seems to be a lot of unearthed dirt and stone around,
heaped upon the floor. You feel uneasy about this place.

Exits.Description: Looks like a dragon trick up ahead ...
The tunnel slopes along, downhill
A stone slab covers the way down.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The dirt and stone are piled up around a large iron ring in the
floor. You can see the outline of a trapdoor!

They stop very abruptly here, right where the piles of
earth begin, it seems.

The floor up ahead looks...strange.  You don't think going ahead
would be a good idea.

Rooms.Name: Pit
Rooms.Description:
You fall through the illusionary floor. You hit the poisoned spikes
below. You die very slowly of blood loss, your head impaled at an
awkward angle.

Exits.Description: Ha!

Rooms.Name: Sloping Tunnel
Rooms.Description:
This tunnel slopes deep, down into the mountain's heart. The air
feels still and uncomfortably warm, despite the closeness of the cave's
entrance above you. There's a deep, musky odor in the air, and the
giant claw marks continue downwards.

Rooms.Name: Sloping Tunnel
Rooms.Description:
A bright light greets your eyes from the north, in direct contrast
to the darkness of the tunnel overhead. You break out in a sweat due to
the overwhelming warmth of the air. The musky odor has grown quite
intense, drowning out everything else in the air and making it hard to
breathe.  Something in your gut begins squirming uncomfortably as you
wonder what's ahead...

Exits.Description: *Sniff!!*  Hmm .... smells like ... could it be ... ?
The darkness of a mountain tunnel obscures your vision.

Rooms.Name: Lair
Rooms.Description:
This place is huge!!! It should be considering the dragon's great
bulk.  However, instead of seeing the customary carnage and mound of
gold that one is accustomed to seeing in a dragon lair, this one is
decorated subtly with tapestries and drapes, and other comforts of
human life. There is even a huge-dragon sized bed--undoubtedly conjured
to life by its elder dragon owner.

Exits.Description:
Head south in a hurry!  Dragons' breath is bad news for a delicate 
adventurer's body.

Rooms.Name: A Hallway in Stanneg Inn
Rooms.Description:
The fading wallpaper was once a bright blue striped with gold, but
now both colors have faded to duller hues.  There are pictures of some
of the original settlers of Stanneg-in-the-Mountains, and a bedraggled
ivy sits on a small cherrywood plantstand.  Three rooms lead off this
end of the hallway, and the receptionist is just west of here.

Exits.Description: A plain brown door leads to one of the inn's bedchambers.
A plain brown door leads to one of the inn's larger chambers.
A plain brown door leads to one of the inn's (usually empty) chambers.
A short hallway leads back to the reception area.

Rooms.Name: A Room at the Inn
Rooms.Description:
A small, plain room is dominated by the large four poster bed with
its thick mattress and heavy down comforter.  There is a slightly musty
smell about the room, as if it is most often left unoccupied.  The
fireplace has not been lit for many weeks.  The windows and floor are
quite clean, however, as is the chamberpot which peeks slightly out
from under the bed.

Exits.Description: A plain brown door leads back to the hall.

Rooms.Name: A Large Room at the Inn
Rooms.Description:
A colorful hand-braided rag rug adds a touch of life to this
otherwise rather dismal room.  Large, clean windows look out on the
ever present mountains.  Stanneg is a tiny isolated community, so these
rooms over the tavern are rarely occupied except by the lost and the
occasional itinerant priest or tinker.  The only exit is west to the
hallway.

Exits.Description: A plain brown door leads back to the hall.

Rooms.Name: A Room with a View
Rooms.Description:
Still more mountains stare in at you from a small, curtainless
window in this very bare room.  A very utilitarian wooden table holds a
large bowl and a pitcher full of water for a quick cleanup.  The
striped wallpaper from the hallway has been replaced here by some plain
gray paint.  The exit back to the hallway lies north through a plain
brown door.

Exits.Description: A plain brown door leads back to the hall.

Rooms.Name: A Short Hallway Leading West
Rooms.Description:
Faded blue and gold wallpaper is beginning to peel away from the
walls in patches here, revealing the faded red wallpaper of ages past.
In its heyday, when the mithril miners were thick in the hills the
Stanneg Inn saw a lot of customers.  The mithril played out.  The local
master smith burned out.  Monsters moved into some of the old mines,
bringing their strange one-eyed lackeys with them, and Stanneg by the
Mountains turned into little better than a ghost town.  Doors lead to
rooms north, west and south of here.

Exits.Description: A small brown door opens into a room.
The receptionist is waiting for you to pay.
A small brown door opens into a room.
A large set of double doors leads west.

Rooms.Name: A Small Plain Room at the Inn
Rooms.Description:
A very simple room, and a very small one.  There is a bed, a table
with a pitcher and bowl, a chamberpot tucked neatly under the bed, and
a small window looking out onto mountains.  The door south leads to the
hallway.

Exits.Description: The hallway is on the other side of the door.

Rooms.Name: Plain Room
Rooms.Description:
The walls in this room have been whitewashed, and whatever pictures
once hung have long since been stolen.  An walnut bedstead sits against
the western wall, across from a small commode containing a ceramic
pitcher and bowl painted a pale blue.  The uncurtained windows to the
south offer an unrestricted view of the mountains that surround the
small town.

Exits.Description: The hallway is on the other side of the door.

Rooms.Name: Faded Elegance
Rooms.Description:
By far the grandest room in the inn as well as the largest, this
room has windows on three sides.  To the north, south and west you have
beautiful scenic views of the Stanneg Mountains.  An enormous, canopied
bed is covered in deep blue velvet.  The bare spots in the plush attest
to the inn's having fallen on hard times.  The only exit is to the
east, through double doors.

Exits.Description: The hallway is on the other side of the door.

Rooms.Name: A Grand Road to Rome
Rooms.Description:
Standing just south of the ornate southern gate to rome, the
magnificence of the ancient city awes the casual visitor and Roman
citizen alike.  From here, a few steps north will take you to marble
temples and governmental buildings, magnificent hippodromes with
their chariot races, and the great gladiatorial contests at the
Colusseum.  To the south, the Grand Road leads to foreign lands.

Exits.Description: The grandeur of Rome
Pleasant fields and well-cultivated vineyards

Rooms.Name: A Grand Road through Well-Cultivated Farmland
Rooms.Description:
Neatly tended fields boarder this Grand Roman road to both east
and west.  Wealthy Romans maintain farms and country estates south of
rome, and the produce adds considerably to their wealth.  Occasionally,
you will see a procession of soldiers headed off to war, or perhaps a
triumphal procession heading home.

Exits.Description: Approaching Rome
Pastoral Countryside

Rooms.Name: Pastoral Countryside
Rooms.Description:
The road bends here around a vineyard filled with ripe, lucious
grapes.  Slaves working the fields look up from their work as you pass.
To the north the grand gates of Rome beckon in the distance.  To the
west the road continues past green fields and villas.

Exits.Description: North towards Rome
West towards parts unknown

Rooms.Name: Rolling hills
Rooms.Description:
A well tended road curves slowly down a westward-descending slope,
and you can see the tall peaks of the Stanneg Mountains in the distant
west.  Around you lie the farms of less wealthy Romans.  Beside the
vineyards lie fields of marrow and other vegetables ripening for the
roman market.

Exits.Description: The road bends
Downhill slowly

Rooms.Name: Downhill Towards a River
Rooms.Description:
The road turns here, conforming its curves to the rapidly increasing
descent westwards towards a river.  You can already scent the
unpleasant stench of downriver from a large city.  The farms are small 
here, the fields not as well tended.  Many are littered with large
rocks. To the east lies the Road to Rome.  Southwest of here lies the
river.

Exits.Description: The Road to Rome
Downhill towards a river

Rooms.Name: Goat Pasture
Rooms.Description:
The path has become quite steep here, and you must make your way
with great care.  Goats roam freely here in the mountains.  Some have
even become a bit wild.  The path rises steeply to the north, descends
rapidly going south.

Exits.Description:
The path rises very steeply, curving here and there to avoid
outcroppings of rock.

Far below and to the south you can make out the outlines of a rickety
old bridge.

Rooms.Name: East of A Troll Bridge
Rooms.Description:
Leading eastward is a narrow steep path that twists around boulders
and trees, past scraggly pastures only a mountain goat could love
towards larger, more civilized places.  To the west, a deep, swift
moving river is spanned by a narrow, two plank bridge.

Exits.Description: It's quite a climb up the hill.  Only a goat could love it.
The sound of deep, rushing water comes to you from the west.

Rooms.Name: A Troll Bridge
Rooms.Description:
It is rumored some #ytrolls#N have taken up residence beneath this
bridge.  Others say this is just a plot to get more money to pay for
Roman extravagances.  Certainly a proper Roman bridge wouldn't
tolerate #ytrolls#N beneath it.  The bridge is wide and long,
however, and there really doesn't seem to be any other way across the
wide river known as the Tiber.  A steep embankment leads down to a
narrow bank by the river.

#GA sign sits in a prominent position before the bridge.#N

Exits.Description: The Road to Rome
The Road to Stanneg
Under the Bridge

Rooms.Name: Under the Troll Bridge
Rooms.Description:
It is clear that someone very large has been camping here,
probably for quite some time.  Perhaps some homeless #ytroll#N.  From
the stories you were told as a child you can remember that they are
fond of UnderBridges ... and chomping on anybody who dares to cross
them!  Now might be a good time to turn back!

Exits.Description: The dim recesses of the underbridge are faintly lit by a cookfire.
A steep embankment leads up to a bridge

Rooms.Name: The UnderBridge
Rooms.Description:
The smell, for non-trolls anyway, is so strong you flinch.  Here and
there you see bits of fur, skin and bones, the remains of young, dead,
not-too-clever billy goats.  A not-very-clean cooking pot rests on a
tripod over an open fire, illuminating the Trolls' Hideaway.

Exits.Description: The river bank with its promise of a sweeter smell beckons you north.

Rooms.Name: Crossing a Troll Bridge
Rooms.Description:
Your footsteps make a hollow, echoing sound crossing this narrow
plank bridge.  There are no strong guard rails to protect you, so you
must be careful on the long walk from one steep pasture to the other.
East leads to Rome (don't all roads?) and west to the mountain village
of Stanneg.

Exits.Description: The road continues east up a steep mountain slope.
The other side of the bridge is simply not close enough!

Rooms.Name: West of a Troll Bridge
Rooms.Description:
A steep embankment leads down to a muddy river that is spashing over
sharp rocks.  You might be able to clamber down the embankment, but it
doesn't look very safe, and there would be no place to stand once you
got there.  To the east lies a narrow bridge spanning the rapidly
rushing water.  Hundreds of years of spring floods have slowly gouged
out this deep trough in the land.  You must either cross the bridge or
ascend the steep slope to the west.
#GA sign calls attention to itself at the edge of the bridge.#N

Exits.Description: The road crosses an old, shaky bridge mainly used now by goats.
An old mining road heads up a steep slope towards a sleepy town.

Rooms.Name: A Forgotten Road to a Forgotten Town
Rooms.Description:
Once this was a broad, well-maintained thoroughfare to a rapidly
growing town high in the mountains.  There are signs that it was
built in a rush, and not by the meticulous and well-trained Romans.

Exits.Description:
The old road winds its way up a steep slope.  Broad pastures of
sweet grass and flowers border the road on both sides.

The road slowly lowers itself onto a troll bridge crossing deep, 
rushing water.

Rooms.Name: Signs of Decay
Rooms.Description:
Once the Stanneg mithril ran out this road fell rapidly into
disuse and decay.  Some of the paving stones were "mined" by farmers
to make fences and others grabbed by local monsters as ammunition.
Oooops!  Did I say ... monsters ???

Exits.Description: The old mining road climbs wearily up the mountain slope.
The high mountain goat pasture rapidly descends to a river.

Rooms.Name: Green Pastures
Rooms.Description:
As the path climbs high into the Stanneg Mountains, the air becomes
thinner and the land around you grows rocky.  Here and there you see
high mountain meadows filled with sweet green grass and, in the spring,
lovely flowers.  The path rises to the north, descends to the south.

Exits.Description: Mountain meadows thin somewhat as you approach a small town.
Thick sweet grass covers a steep mountainside.

Rooms.Name: Near a Small Cottage
Rooms.Description:
On the outskirts of Stanneg lies a small cottage owned by one of the
original settlers in this area.  Stanneg, known now as a former mining
town, was once a simple community of people ekeing out their existance
in a very remote location.  The road to town leads north.  Larger
cities may be found downhill from here.

Exits.Description: A lovely grass covered slope leads downhill.
A few scattered, dusty buildings form this old town.

Mobs.Name: farmer m9900 m99
Mobs.LongDescription: A farmer walks around, awed by all there is to do in Stanneg.
Mobs.Description:
This farmer is a resident of Stanneg by the Mountains, and as such, is
one of the most boring people on earth.  Every day is pretty much the
same for him.  You wonder who is feeding his chickens while he is
wandering around town.
Mobs.ActionScript: %%5 yawn

Mobs.Name: storekeeper m9901 m99
Mobs.LongDescription: A bored storekeeper waits for you to do something.
Mobs.Description:
The bored storekeeper keeps a lazy eye on you as he waits for you to
buy something.  Whee.

Mobs.Name: Cowgirl m99
Mobs.LongDescription: A cowgirl stands here ready to defend her horses...
Mobs.Description:
This woman seems ready for anything you might do... she is truly a
woman to be reckoned with...

Mobs.Name: horse m9903 m99
Mobs.LongDescription: A horse does horsely things here.
Mobs.Description:
This horse looks like a nice horse.  It looks at you with soft brown
eyes and you want to give it a carrot and tie ribbons in its mane.

Mobs.Name: farmer's farmers wife m9904 m99
Mobs.LongDescription: A farmer's wife offers you some vegetables.
Mobs.Description:
This woman has many different types of fruits and vegetables for you to
buy.  She looks bored, though.

Mobs.Name: Aglandiir dragon prince m9905 m99
Mobs.LongDescription: The Dragon Prince, Aglandiir, sits here looking at you curiously.
Mobs.Description:
Towering over his bodyguards, his scales glistening with a pearlescent
gleam that is somehow neither red nor black, but both together,
depending on the whim of the flickering torchlight.  Aglandiir lives in
the ancestral home of dragonkind, proud and fierce.  He has a taste for
the finer things civilization has to offer, and the cyclops, who toady
to him, are forever bringing him small treasures.  Aglandiir is as
magnificent as his surroundings suggest.

Mobs.Name: Cyclops m9906 m99
Mobs.LongDescription: The cyclops is trying to judge range with no depth perception.
Mobs.Description:
This Cyclops throws rocks real good.  With one eye though, hitting the
target is another matter.  He looks at you and growls as he misses
again!

Mobs.Name: Salle woman m9907 m99
Mobs.LongDescription: A woman ignores you completely, so intent is she upon her sword.
Mobs.Description:
She is a stunning woman, all hair and eyes, it seems.  Her clothing
is of the same tawny brown of her skin and hair.  Her blue eyes look at
you appraisingly, seemingly to show great intelligence.  Her mouth
twitches into a sneer...

Mobs.Name: Duwick man m9908 m99
Mobs.LongDescription: A truly immense man laughs at you, and draws his knife!
Mobs.Description:
This has to be one of the biggest men you've ever seen.  He is a
full seven feet toe to head, and weighs a good three hundred pounds --
mostly on his biceps and pectorals it appears.  An ornate scabbard
slaps by his side, with the pommel of a silvered dagger sticking
out...a tiny weapon for such a large man!

Mobs.Name: Receptionist m9909 m99
Mobs.LongDescription: A receptionist offers you a room.
Mobs.Description:
He looks like a retired farmer now making an honest living in an
inn.  More power to him!

Mobs.Name: innkeeper m9910 m99
Mobs.LongDescription: An aged innkeeper greets you as you enter.
Mobs.Description:
He's old and graying, but seems to have been able to keep his mental
faculties through the years.  A large woolen sweater is wrapped about
him for warmth.  His blue eyes dance with amusement as he notices your
weapons, but he doesn't seem too terribly startled.

Mobs.Name: hunter m9911 m99
Mobs.LongDescription: A hunter strides along purposefully, looking neither right nor left.
Mobs.Description:
He looks mean, as if the very personality of the mountains had
infected him with hardness.  His stride is purposeful, his face
weathered, his eyes cold and dark.  Others are standing out of his way
as he walks on by.
Mobs.ActionScript:
%%5 em lifts his bow, notching in an arrow.;%5 em takes careful aim
 down the shaft of his bow.

Mobs.Name: waiter m9912 m99
Mobs.LongDescription: A waiter rushes by, intent on his business.
Mobs.Description:
He looks harried from the way he hastily takes orders and rushes in
the back to get food, and to the bar for drinks.  He doesn't even spare
you a glance as he passes by.

Mobs.Name: waitress m9913 m99
Mobs.LongDescription: A waitress rushes by, intent on her business.
Mobs.Description:
She looks married from the way she hastily takes orders and rushes
in the back to get food, and to the bar for drinks.  She doesn't even
spare you a glance as she passes by.

Mobs.Name: bartender m9914 m99
Mobs.LongDescription: A bartender washes a glass idly here.
Mobs.Description:
He nods, smiles, and asks you what you would like to drink.  As you
decide, he slowly polishes a glass with an old bar rag.  The glass is
completely clean, but he polishes it anyway.  Go figure.

Mobs.Name: bandit m9915 m99
Mobs.LongDescription: A bandit springs into action upon seeing you.
Mobs.Description:
Whew!  Has this guy ever seen a bath?  His face, hands, arms...
nearly every bit of him is covered with grime, dust, dirt and decay.
His sword is polished and cleaned though...

Mobs.Name: bandit guard m9916 m99
Mobs.LongDescription: A bandit guard stands at attention here.
Mobs.Description:
He may be a bandit, but he's no slacker.  You wonder who would be
able to keep these bandits in line enough to pull a good guard duty...
(Boy is this guy DIRTY!!!)

Mobs.Name: miner worker slave m9917 m99
Mobs.LongDescription: A slave here is mining out a new passageway.
Mobs.Description:
The slave looks up at you with pleading eyes.  He wants his freedom.
The chains around his ankles are tight, and you wonder if you should
set him free, and if you even can.

Mobs.Name: farmer m9918 m99
Mobs.LongDescription: A farmer walks around, looking for something to do.
Mobs.Description:
This farmer is a resident of Stanneg by the Mountains, and as such, is
one of the most boring people on earth.

Mobs.Name: hunter m9919 m99
Mobs.LongDescription: A hunter walks through the town streets on his own time.
Mobs.Description:
He looks mean, as if the very personality of the mountains had
infected him with hardness.  His stride is purposeful, his face
weathered, his eyes cold and dark.  Others are standing out of his way
as he walks on by.

Mobs.Name: apple grower m9920 m99
Mobs.LongDescription: The apple grower is in town for the day, looking for excitement.
Mobs.Description:
Tinted slightly green from eating too many green apples, this
half-orc is unimpressed with the sights and sounds of the tiny town of
Stanneg.  Perhaps he will start raising sheep for company instead of
apple trees.

Mobs.Name: chambermaid m9921 m99
Mobs.LongDescription: The little wood elf chambermaid is just too cute for words.
Mobs.Description:
Well, the forest was just too boring, so the little elf hired on as
a chambermaid at the Stanneg Inn, in Stanneg.  She is young, pretty and
full of mischief.  She just wants to have fun.

Mobs.Name: horse rancher m9922 m99
Mobs.LongDescription: The half-orc horse rancher rode into town on his horse, Joe.
Mobs.Description:
One of many horse ranchers / traders who live outside the small
rural town of Stanneg, this rancher raises warhorses for the many
knights.  He turns a tidy profit at it!

Mobs.Name: highwayman m9923 m99
Mobs.LongDescription: Although this is no highway, the highwayman will rob you just the same!
Mobs.Description:
Although this path looks forgotten, it was once a major thoroughfare
between a major mining community (Stanneg by the Mountains) and the
thriving metropolis of Midgaard (by the Sea).  The highwaymen have not
forgotten! They will roam this path til they die!

Mobs.Name: one-eyed jack m9924 m99
Mobs.LongDescription: "Stand and deliver!", shouts One-eyed Jack.
Mobs.Description:
The most feared of the highwaymen, One-Eyed Jack is ruthless and
cunning.  He's mean and he's evil.  And that one eye is right in the
middle of his forehead, making you think he's not quite right in the
head.
Mobs.ActionScript: %%3 smirk

Mobs.Name: guest m9925 m99
Mobs.LongDescription: "How dare you barge in here!" screams the guest of the inn.
Mobs.Description:
Well, can you blame him?  He paid for this rather shabby but
expensive room, and was all set to take a nice hot bath in the large
copper tub when you come barging in where you are obviously not wanted!
Mobs.ActionScript: %%5 scream

Mobs.Name: Nelly mindslayer m99 m9926
Mobs.LongDescription: Nelly the Mind Bogglingly Magnificent Mindslayer tours Stanneg.
Mobs.Description:
Nelly used to tour Major Capitals of the World!! (especially those
beginning with the letter "S")  She had a show of amazing "Feats of the
Magnificent Mind of the #gGnomish#N Miss Nelly!", however greater and
more wondrous mages were soon envious of the fortune she amassed with
her tour, and she was, alas, outclassed.  She now tours Small Towns of
the World!! (especially those beginning with the letter "S")

Mobs.Name: O'rgile xorgyle minotaur m99 m9927
Mobs.LongDescription: The town's only doctor is a fierce #RMinotaur#Y named O'Rgile.
Mobs.Description:
Lust for blood sent this sharp-horned Minotaur to war as a mercenary.
He grew sad, losing so many of his comrades to battles, and vowed to
learn to heal as well as to kill.  He still has a pretty mean horn,
however, and he is not at all afraid to use it.

Mobs.Name: O'Degra xodegra m9928 m99
Mobs.LongDescription: O'Degra may be short, stocky and a bit furry, but he is quite strong.
Mobs.Description:
O'Degra was the original lone Irish Dwarven miner to discover the seams
of mithril running through the mountains here in Stanneg.  He became
quite wealthy from his fabulous discovery, but he gave it all away and
now is quite poor.  He still roams the hills looking for another "find".

Mobs.Name: high sheriff m9929 m99
Mobs.LongDescription: The High Sheriff of Stanneg eyes you, fingering his badge of office.
Mobs.Description:
If ever a political appointee there was, there was the High Sheriff of
Stanneg.  His heavy gold badge rests on his velvet-covered paunch.
Heavy eyebrows meet in the middle of a low forehead, and his scent is
faintly reminiscent of troll.  With bandits living near here, cyclops
roaming the hills, highwaymen on trail leading here and rumors of a
Dragon Prince living not far away, the Sheriff has clearly NOT been
doing a good job!
Mobs.ActionScript:
%%5 em fingers his badge of office thoughtfully.;
%5 rubs his palms over his enormous velvet clad belly.

Mobs.Name: deputy dahwig m9930 m99
Mobs.LongDescription: Deputy Dahwig just can't seem to get his sword sheathed properly.
Mobs.Description:
Dressed in tattered trousers with a sword by his side, Deputy Sheriff
Dahwig is just the picture of incompetence.  He frequently misses the
scabbard for his sword, and adds yet another tear to his battered
clothing or a slight gash to his skin.

Mobs.Name: aunt auntie tabitha m9931 m99
Mobs.LongDescription: Auntie Tabitha keeps her cookie jar full for children who visit.
Mobs.Description:
Auntie Tabitha is kind of an institution here in Stanneg.  She came here
as a young bride decades before the mining explosion.  She has vowed
never to leave, although Stanneg has become known for being "the most
boring town on earth".
Mobs.ActionScript:
%%5 em asks, "Wanna cookie, honey ?";
%1 em asks, "Want some honey, cookie ?

Mobs.Name: troll mean ol ugly m9932 m99
Mobs.LongDescription: A bridge troll wonders if you will fit in her cooking pot.
Mobs.Description:
Ever since a run in with a certain very LARGE billy goat gruff, this
troll has gone hungry.  She has been just waiting for someone to come
discover her little hidey hole and volunteer to be her dinner.  She
thanks you for volunteering.

Mobs.Name: billygoat wee little billy goat gruff m9933 m99
Mobs.ShortDescription: a wee little billy goat gruff
Mobs.LongDescription: A wee little billy goat gruff looks for some sweet meadow grass.
Mobs.Description:
A very tiny billy goat with a tiny white beard treads lightly, looking
for some sweet grass to eat.  He and his many billy goat brothers and
sisters feast on the grass on both sides of this small mountain canyon.
Mobs.ActionScript: %%5 em nudges you gently with his little head.

Mobs.Name: billygoat billy goat middle middle-sized gruff m9934 m99
Mobs.LongDescription: The middle-sized billy goat gruff says, "Wait for my big brother!"
Mobs.Description:
The medium-sized billy goat wears a medium-sized bell on a medium-sized
leather collar around his medium sized billy goat gruff neck.  He is
getting tired of being medium sized, neither cute like his littlest
brothers, nor strong like his bigger brothers.
Mobs.ActionScript: %%5 em headbutts you none too gently.  Ouch!! That hurt!!!

Mobs.Name: billygoat billy goat enormous gruff m9935 m99
Mobs.LongDescription: The biggest billy goat gruff has two long, curved, sharp, wicked horns.
Mobs.Description:
The enormous billy goat is a threat even (perhaps especially) to trolls.
A force to be reckoned with!  He could gore you with one of his horns,
or simply ram you down in a fierce headbutt.
Mobs.ActionScript:
%%5 emote rams into you from behind, knocking you to the ground!;
%1 say Where's that troll been messin with my brothers?

Mobs.Name: gnome tourist m9936 m99
Mobs.LongDescription: The #gGnome#Y came to record the former glory of Stanneg for Glob, Inc.
Mobs.Description:
This little gnome is fascinated by history.  The Descent of Stanneg from
prosperous mining town to this boring little place amazed her both for
its rapidity and its completeness.  She is talking to some of the
town's long time residents, planning to amaze her friends back at the
Glob, Inc. Information headquarters.
Mobs.ActionScript: %%5 peer

Mobs.Name: fat friar francis m9937 m99
Mobs.LongDescription: Fat Friar Francis watches you from shifty eyes.
Mobs.Description:
Friar Francis has a passion for the good things of life, and
unfortunately has not the means to indulge in them.  How does he pay for
them then ?  Nobody knows for sure, but it is rumored he has a link with
the bandits living in caves near here.
Mobs.ActionScript: %%5 cast 'create waybread'

Mobs.Name: kithy boy little sturdy m9938 m99
Mobs.LongDescription: A sturdy little boy begs for choco cookies.
Mobs.Description:
A very tall little boy with deep blue eyes looks up at you appealingly.
He has short, straight blond hair and an engaging smile.  You can sense
he's very good at scrounging cookies from the town's best cookie-bakers!
Mobs.ActionScript: %%5say Gimme cookie!  Kithy want choco!

Mobs.Name: granny higglebottom m9939 m99
Mobs.LongDescription: Granny Higglebottom's daughter has left to work in the valley.
Mobs.Description:
Ever since Granny Higglebottom's daughter went to work for "the Royals",
Granny H has been lonely, cranky and out of sorts.  Her thin, wispy
white hair forms a soft halo around her deeply lined face.

Mobs.Name: sara m9940 m99 xsarastro
Mobs.LongDescription: Long curly hair falls gracefully around the face of Stro's sister Sara.
Mobs.Description:
Stro's twin sister Sara looks very much like her brother, except for her
long curly hair.  She and Stro are constantly together, and constantly
in trouble for some piece of mischief or another.  It is a full time job
for their big sister Rooth to keep an eye on them!

Mobs.Name: stro m9941 xsarastro m99
Mobs.LongDescription: Stro looks up at you through bright, mischievous green eyes.
Mobs.Description:
Pale blond hair cut very short gives this athletic little boy a slightly
elfin look.  He and his twin sister Sara are active, curious children.

Mobs.Name: rooth xrue m9942 m99
Mobs.LongDescription: Rooth often takes the twins for walks through the hills near Stanneg.
Mobs.Description:
Rooth loves her twin brother and sister, Sara and Stro, even though
their mischievous nature often lands all three of them in trouble.  The
three of them live on a farm outside Stanneg, where their family raises
goats for both the wool and the milk.

Mobs.Name: floyd m9943 xkalsa m99
Mobs.LongDescription: Floyd sings madrigals in in tight leather pants and a #mpink#Y shirt.
Mobs.Description:
Remember when you were young, you shone like the sun
Now there's a look in your eyes, like black holes in the sky
You were caught in the crossfire of childhood and stardom
Blown on the steel breeze
Come on you target for far away laughter, come on you stranger,
you legend, you martyr, and shine!
You reached for the secret too soon
You cried for the moon
Shine on you crazy diamond
Mobs.ActionScript: %%5 airguitar

Mobs.Name: troll mean ol ugly m9944 m99
Mobs.LongDescription: The bridge troll is drawn to you, drooling, dreaming of soup!
Mobs.Description:
You sure look good enough to eat! At least to *this* troll.  But
don't let it go to your head.  He's so hungry he'd eat just about
anything!

Mobs.Name: farmer's farmers wife m9905 m99
Mobs.LongDescription: A farmer's wife came to town to see the sights.
Mobs.Description:
After endless days and endless nights on one of the most boring farms in
the world, finally the farmer's wife gets to come to town to see the
sights.

Mobs.Name: Grizzly Gus m99 m9946
Mobs.LongDescription:
Grizzly Gus, the mountain man, he'll be roamin these mountains as long
as he can.
Mobs.Description:
Grizzly Gus is a nasty old cuss.  He smells like he hasn't had a bath in
years, which he probably hasn't.  He doesn't see the need.  Gus is
happiest ALONE in his mountains.
Mobs.ActionScript: %%15say GIT!!

Mobs.Name: Helmet xhelm m9947 m99 m9947
Mobs.LongDescription: #GGrandpa H's mining helmet glows demonically in a corner, forgotten.#N
Mobs.Description:
A very large green helmet with a large glowing crystal sits quietly in a
corner.  During its heyday, all miners in Stanneg owned one of these
helmets.  It is very sturdy, providing a good deal of protection from
falling rocks, and the crystal provides a handy source of light for the
miners.  This particular one, however, looks somewhat ... demonic,
despite the eerie feline reflection in its surface.  

Grandpa Higglebottom (sadly no longer with us) was at the helm of the
Stanneg Mining and Exploration Company, a once profitable subdivision of
Glob, Inc.

Mobs.Name: music box xmelody m99 m9948
Mobs.LongDescription: #GThe music box plays a pretty little melody.#N
Mobs.Description:
Crank up this music box with the wind-up arm and it will play a lovely
little song.  You have heard this tune before, but where ?

Mobs.Name: bodyguard m99 m9949
Mobs.LongDescription: The prince's bodyguard is a dark and glorious dragon.
Mobs.Description:
Only the strongest, most fearsome dragons are allowed to guard the heir
to the dragon throne, Prince Aglandiir.  This one is deepest black,
except for the glowing golden eyes and the occasional tongue of flame.

Mobs.Name: prospector m99 m9950
Mobs.LongDescription: The wiry little gnomish prospector searches endlessly for mithril.
Mobs.Description:
Determined to strike it rich in the mountains around Stanneg, confident
that the bandits won't bother him since he is so poor, the prospector
searches the hills and caves of the Stanneg mountains for hints of
mithril.
Mobs.ActionScript: %%15say I know you! you're one o'them claim jumpers!;%10 glare

Mobs.Name: man spry guy ol mountain m99 m9951
Mobs.LongDescription: The spry old guy hides away on the mountain side.
Mobs.Description:
Long years away from people has made the old coot even more distrustful
of the rest of the two-legged world than he was before.  He's living off
the bare pickings of the land, killing wild goats and squirrels, and
eating greens that others might call weeds.  His temper, like his breath
and his body odor, is most foul.

Mobs.Name: wheel spinning m99 m9952 mimic
Mobs.LongDescription: #GThe spinning wheel twirls hypnotically, entrancing you.
Mobs.Description:
Auntie Tabitha says she uses this lovely old walnut spinning wheel to
spin yarn for Granny Higglebottom.  There is something not quite RIGHT
about Auntie T, however.  But nothing wrong with the goats, aside from
a little mischievous headbutting.  The goats roam the mountain valley
between here and Rome, and are gathered twice annually to be sheared.
The goathair is then spun into soft yarn.  Granny H has a passion for
soft knitted blankets, and has managed to capture a bit of tourist trade
selling them.

Mobs.Name: explorer orcish m99 m9953
Mobs.LongDescription: The Orcish explorer is searching for new lands and peoples to conquer.
Mobs.Description:
The Orc explorer has left his cave to look for newer, larger caves here
in the played out mines of Stanneg.  If he happens to find one with a
bit of mithril left, look out! He will be making some pretty scary
weapons.

Mobs.Name: wolf cub xnightwolf playful wolfcub m99 m9954
Mobs.LongDescription: An adorable little wolf cub romps around in the sweet grass.
Mobs.Description:
Thick jet-black fur covers this adorable little wolf cub.  He has
wandered away from his den for a frolic in the sunshine and adventures
chasing goats ... and perhaps chasing adventurers as well!

Mobs.Name: guest phobic xphobos m9955
Mobs.LongDescription: The slightly phobic guest of the Inn clutches the sheets in worry.
Mobs.Description:
The poor guest quakes at the thought of the mountains around him.  What
if there is a quake?  And he is a bit nervous around goats ... and there
are so many of them.  So many phobias, hard to pick which one to worry
over!

Mobs.Name: guest raven-haired xraven m9956 woman
Mobs.LongDescription: The raven-haired guest looks about her warily.
Mobs.Description:
She does her best to sooth her phobic companion, but finds it difficult
at times.  The guest has long, thick black hair, and an air of constant
awareness, a stirring restlessness that reminds you of a wild creature.
For some reason the wolfcub you passed on your way into Stanneg comes to
mind, as does the glimpse you had of some graceful, feral movement in
the trees.

Objects.Name: orange o99
Objects.Description: An orange lies on the ground here.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: You wonder how it got here, seeing how oranges are non-migratory.

Objects.Name: bale wheat o99
Objects.Description: There is a bale of wheat here.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
It doesn't look appetizing to you, but
a horse might enjoy this...

Objects.Name: zither o99
Objects.Description: A HUGE zither made of gold rests in the corner

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Someone truly huge with big fingers might be able to play this.  You
can't.

Objects.Name: barrel perfume
Objects.Description: You can smell a barrel on the other side of the room from here.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Smells good...the label reads:
   "Somewhere between GPA and MUD there lies...
		OBSESSION"

Objects.Name: statue
Objects.Description: There is a statue of Aglandiir here, made of solid gold.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: He's a pretty striking chap, for a dragon.

Objects.Name: Halberd
Objects.Description: A runed halberd lies on the ground here.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The runes glow with a bright light, making you
think that this might be a pretty decent weapon.

Objects.Name: potion protection dun vial
Objects.Description: A vial of a dun fluid is here.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: Looks thick, and brownish-grey (dun).  Ick!

Objects.Name: crown
Objects.Description: Aglandiir's crown sits here, radiating a shield.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The shield repulses you, making you wonder how
you're going to get your hands on this huge, valuble
chunk of gold...

Objects.Name: apple
Objects.Description: A scrawny red apple sits here.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: Its not wormy...yet.

Objects.Name: bread loaf
Objects.Description: A fresh loaf of Ry bread lies here.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: Mmmm...Ry!

Objects.Name: melon
Objects.Description: A melon sits here, discarded evidently.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: Wow!  Look at the size of that melon!

Objects.Name: knife
Objects.Description: An exquisitely crafted knife rests here.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The craftsmanship...it takes your breath away!  This knife...it had
to have been forged by the legendary smith Gabadiel.  It must be worth a
fortune!

Objects.Name: sword long
Objects.Description: A superb long sword sticks in the earth.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
This sword is light, but the heft is perfectly balanced.  Such an
incredible weapon can only have be crafted by the legendary smith
Gabadiel, and as such be worth a fortune!

Objects.Name: sword short
Objects.Description: A short sword lies here...a work of art!

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
It brings tears to your eyes.  This must have been Gabadiel the
smith's masterpiece, his final work.  Simply invaluble.

Objects.Name: corpse
Objects.Description: A dismembered and burnt corpse lies on the ground here.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: It's still smouldering a little; the culprits can't be far off!

Objects.Name: scimitar
Objects.Description: A scimitar as long as your arm lies here.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: This weapon really isn't of too high a quality.

Objects.Name: crate
Objects.Description: A crate is stacked here.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: It's a standard wooden crate.

Objects.Name: hunting knife
Objects.Description: a hunting knife lies here, unwanted

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
This is the type of weapon you would use to bag some deer or rabbits,
but not the type you'd take into battle...

Objects.Name: vest leather
Objects.Description: A nice leather vest lies here.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: The seams are delicately sewn with a enruned thread...

Objects.Name: glass
Objects.Description: A glass of beer sits forgotten here.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
A nice glass filled with homebrew.  There doesn't seem to be too much
stuff floating in it.

Objects.Name: glass
Objects.Description: A big glass of mead sits here, cool and frosty.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: Looks good.  Looks warm.  Doesn't matter, it still looks good.

Objects.Name: shot
Objects.Description: A shot of whiskey is sitting here.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: Whew!  Looks like potent stuff!

Objects.Name: bag
Objects.Description: A small bag.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: This is a standard bag.

Objects.Name: candle
Objects.Description: A candle lies here, unlit.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: A home-made candle, how quaint!

Objects.Name: nail
Objects.Description: A penny nail lies in the dust.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: Its a common iron nail, used for carpentry work.

Objects.Name: pot
Objects.Description: A cast-iron pot sits on the ground.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: It's a nice pot.  You could use it, if you ever settled down.

Objects.Name: rusty sword
Objects.Description: A fairly poorly balanced sword is not well hidden.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: Clearly Gabadiel's work, and just as clearly not his best.

Objects.Name: silver sword
Objects.Description: Gabadiel crafted this sword of purest silver.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: Clearly Gabadiel's work, and just as clearly not his best.

Objects.Name: letter parchment
Objects.Description: A piece of foolscap soft as cloth has some faded writing.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The writing is faded and spidery, clearly scrawled in haste, however you
can just barely make out a few words.

         #r    I will ... survive the assault but they will not ... 
             my treasure ... hidden securely ... tree

Objects.Name: amulet
Objects.ShortDescription: an amulet shaped like a sword
Objects.Description: A silver amulet is attached to a silver chain.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The amulet is engraved with the emblem of a sword and a large "G".
Clearly the work of the master craftsman, Gabadiel.

Objects.Name: corpse
Objects.Description: What appears to be a burnt log turns out to be a charred corpse.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Alas, apparently this still smouldering body was quite recently alive
and well.  Who could have done this dastardly deed?

Objects.Name: strongbox box iron
Objects.Description: Faintly, in the shadows, you can see a large box bound in iron.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
A large box of some dark wood is bound with strong straps of iron and
locked with a HUGE padlock.  Clearly there is something very valuable
hidden away here.

Objects.Name: tub copper bath
Objects.Description: Steam rises from a large copper tub sitting in front of the fireplace.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
An enormous copper bathing tub has been filled two-thirds of the way up
with steaming hot water.  The tub is large enough to bathe even Duwick,
an IMMENSE man who frequently rents a room at this inn.

Objects.Name: troll shirt proud
Objects.ShortDescription: a #yProud to be a Troll#N shirt
Objects.Description: A large smelly shirt says, "#YProud to be #yTrollish#Y!!#G"

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
A large shirt has a loud sign on it.  The writing says ...
 
                    #YProud to be a #yTroll#Y!!!#N

Objects.Name: cookie choco chocolate
Objects.Description: A dark, not-too-sweet chocolate cookie would melt in your mouth.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Deep dark chocolate cookies are Aunt Tabitha's favorites to make, and
Kithy's favorites to eat.  They are just the right size for his little
hands to hold and to cram into his little-boy mouth.
^

Objects.Name: cookie jar cookiejar
Objects.ShortDescription: a very large ceramic cookie jar
Objects.Description: A ceramic jar shaped like a large-bellied gnome is filled with cookies.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Grasp the ears to lift off the head, and inside you will see dozens of
cookies of all varieties.  There are chocolate ones, peanut butter
cookies, sugar cookies, oatmeal cookies and many many more.  It's a
magical jar that is never empty, full of cookies that are never stale.

Objects.Name: strawberry
Objects.Description: A small deep red strawberry promises to have intense and sweet flavor.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The Stanneg mountains are primarily known for the mithril mines that
once played such an important role in the local economy, and for the
dullness of the town of Stanneg itself.  The sweet wild strawberries
that grow on the hillsides are an unexpected treat.

Objects.Name: chair rocking wooden
Objects.Description: A large wooden rocking chair creaks slowly back and forth on its own.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Built to last in the heyday of Stanneg, this is a very solid, very large
rocking chair built, perhaps, for one of the Troll mothers who came to
mine the mithril.  It will be here long after you are gone.

Objects.Name: stump
Objects.Description: A blackened stump is all that remains of a once large tree.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
About waist high (to an adult human), the stump is black and sooty, and
it is difficult to tell what kind of tree this once was.

Objects.Name: towel
Objects.Description: A large soft blue towel has been neatly folded and left.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
A soft fluffy towel can be used to dry you off after you've bathed,
or wrapped around you if you have unexpected visitors.

Objects.Name: shirt trollish
Objects.Description: A very large shirt says, "#rKiss me! #gI'm #yTrollish#Y!!!#G"

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
An shirt with writing on it.  The writing says ...
 
                    #rKiss me! #gI'm #yTrollish#Y!!!#N

Objects.Name: badge office
Objects.ShortDescription: the High Sheriff's Badge of Office
Objects.Description: The High Sheriff of Stanneg by the Mountains lost his Badge of Office.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
A very ornate mithril badge has been suspended from a long silver 
chain.  The front of the badge has been inscribed with the Insignia of
the Great Council of Stanneg.  On the back, someone has scratched in
very tiny letters:
 
                    #YTroll Power#N

Objects.Name: gauntlets
Objects.Description: A pair of very large gauntlets are engraved with "#yTroll POWER#Y!!#G"

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Troll gauntlets have been inscribed wit hthe magic words ...
 
                    #yTroll POWER#N!!!#N

Objects.Name: magic cape nellys stanneg
Objects.Description: A swirl of glitter dazzles the eye.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Nelly's magic cape flows along darkly behind her.  Although it would be
hiplength on a human, on Nelly, the cape just covers her ankles.  As she
walks, the cape flutters near her feet.  The cape is a deep purple,
covered with a swirly pattern made up of the letter "S" repeated in all
sizes in all directions.

Objects.Name: sneaky boots kithys
Objects.Description: Kithy's sneaky boots sneaked away from him!

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Kithy has a special friend in the mountains that nobdy knows about,
especially his Aunt Tabitha (with whom he lives).  She is a witch with a
fondness for little boys!  and for his last birthday, she added a
special enchantment to these very quiet boots.  Kithy ALWAYS shares his
cookies with her.

Objects.Name: blanket angora stanneg
Objects.Description: Granny Higglebottom hand knit a soft dark gray blanket of angora wool.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The little goats that roam the mountain hillsides are prized for their
soft angora wool.  Granny Higglebottom washes, spins, dyes and knits the
wool into beautiful blankets and sweaters to sell to the tourist trade.
This blanket is very thick and warm in the winter, but soft and cozy to
the touch.  It has been dyed soft mottled shades of a heathery gray.

Objects.Name: helmet mining
Objects.Description: A dusty mining helmet has a glowing crystal to light your way.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Mithril is mined from deep within the mountains, and miners need both 
protection from falling rock and a strong source of light.  This handy 
helmet provides both.  The helmet still carries a price tag stuck to the
back.
It says, #y116 gold#N.

Objects.Name: gold coins
Objects.Description: A small stash of gold is partially hidden from your eyes.

Objects.Name: gold coins
Objects.Description: A large horde of gold has been stashed away here.

Objects.Name: bed iron bedstead o99
Objects.Description: A feather mattress makes the huge cast iron bed look comfy.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Covered with sheets yellowing with age, a few hard pillows, and a down
comforter, this bed may not be the most comfortable place to spend the
night, but it is pure luxury compared to miner's accomodations in the
hills.
